questions.author: CC-Mac
questions.question: Why wasn't the cbBTC/WETH position moved to Aerodrome, even though its interface showed a far higher APR than Uniswap?
questions.reference: Checked on 08.09: on Aerodrome a position staked in the gauge earns only AERO emissions (the fees go to voters), and the displayed emission APR is computed on liquidity staked in the active tick ±1 tick, a band of about 0.3%. A ±40% position holds about 0.5% of that liquidity, so it would earn roughly 4 to 6% a year in AERO, a token with about 10.9% yearly inflation, against roughly 5 to 11% a year in fees on Uniswap with no token to sell. The LP crowd on Aerodrome sits about 10x tighter, so a wide position gets crumbs; the advantage exists only for ultra-narrow, actively managed positions, the class the project had falsified in late August. Verdict: no, Uniswap stays the venue for the wide position.

facts.a: a staked Aerodrome position earns only AERO emissions; the fees go to voters
facts.b: the displayed emission APR is computed on liquidity in the active tick ±1 (about a 0.3% band); a ±40% position holds about 0.5% of it, about 4-6%/yr in AERO
facts.c: Uniswap at ±40% gives about 5-11%/yr in fees with no token to sell (AERO inflates about 10.9%/yr)
facts.d: the advantage exists only for ultra-narrow, actively managed positions, a class already falsified in late August
facts.e: verdict 08.09: no; Uniswap stays the venue for the wide position on this pair

questions.author: CC-Mac
questions.question: When the bot raised a downtrend alarm on the product pools, why was the default advice to sign nothing?
questions.reference: The FlatWide hybrid was chosen knowing it holds market beta, so a DOWN signal was treated as information, not an order. The data of 26 to 27.08 (more than 40 walk-forward and full-period runs) showed that exiting on the trend signal on average worsens the result against holding the wide LP, because the signal comes late, the exit costs money and the rebounds are missed; cash wins only in strong, long crashes of about -28 to -41%, which cannot be recognised in advance. A hedge (option A) or an exit to cash (option B, only on hard criteria) remained available.

questions.author: CC-Mac
questions.question: When was the product run through a Monte Carlo simulation, and how did it come out against HODL?
questions.reference: On 01.09: 5000 paths of 90 days, a block bootstrap from 500 days of daily ETH and BTC prices with the full v3 mechanics of both legs. From $5,765 the median ended at $5,950 (+3.2%), with a 57% chance of a gain; against HODL the median was -$125 and the chance of beating HODL 36%, consistent with the historical gates. The profile is asymmetric: in calm markets the strategy wins about $50 to 100 over HODL from fees, in a crash it loses about $500 to 1,100, 'selling insurance against boredom'.

questions.author: CC-Mac
questions.question: What does usdValueViaPool do, and why was it added?
questions.reference: A UI function added on 01.09 in usePortfolio.ts. The cockpit card of the cbBTC/WETH position showed accrued fees of $0.00 although about $0.70 had accrued, because usdValueOf cannot value a pair without a stable leg (it returns null) and the fee value defaulted to 0. usdValueViaPool converts the unknown leg at the pool price (sqrtPriceX96) into the ETH or stable leg and then into USD; it is used for both the position value and the fees, and the old '(bot valuation)' fallback disappeared.

questions.author: CC-Mac
questions.question: What does an UNMAPPED verdict mean in the candidate funnel?
questions.reference: The funnel validates pools from the DefiLlama ranking, and first maps each one to its on-chain address through a dictionary of known major tokens per network, factory.getPool and a sanity check of token0/token1. When a token is outside the dictionary or the sanity check disagrees, the verdict is UNMAPPED: the pool goes to manual review and the funnel never guesses an address or runs on silently wrong data. Exotic pairs without an ETH/BTC or stable leg are UNMAPPED by rule. Eligibility and OPEN proposals skip FAIL and UNMAPPED pools. In the first full backfill (25.08) all 5 candidates were mapped, zero UNMAPPED.

facts.a: the verdict when a ranked pool cannot be mapped to its on-chain address (token outside the dictionary of majors, or the token0/token1 sanity check disagrees); manual review, the funnel never guesses addresses
facts.b: exotic pairs without an ETH/BTC or stable leg are UNMAPPED by rule
facts.c: eligibility and OPEN proposals skip FAIL and UNMAPPED pools
facts.d: in the first full backfill (25.08) all 5 candidates were mapped, zero UNMAPPED

questions.author: owner
questions.question: How was the option of confirming transactions done technically, that is, what happened after clicking to confirm the creation of a new LP position?
questions.reference: The corpus records two paths. The one used for real positions is the cockpit: an OPEN proposal card has an [Open] button that reads the pool on demand (slot0 and liquidity over RPC) and opens the position window for a new position (no NFT yet). That window reads the wallet's balances and allowances, asks for token approvals where needed and builds the mint with the same functions as the manual add-liquidity form (createPosition and prepareAddLiquidityTransaction, rewritten on the Uniswap SDK on 10.08); before signing, each action switches the wallet to the right network and takes a fresh wallet client, and the owner signs in the wallet (Rabby). For the manual form (AddLiquidity, rewritten 10.08) the journal also records approvals on the exact amounts, an eth_call simulation of the mint before sending and slippage limited to 0.1 to 1%. After signing (fixes of 27.08, from the first real entry) the window waits for the receipt, re-reads balances and allowances, and after a successful mint closes with a toast confirming the new position.
